claim.spatial_precision: Samarkand city castle context; exact castle location unknown
claim.summary: In his 1404 description of Samarkand, Clavijo reports that the city castle held roughly one thousand captives who were skilled workers and were compelled to labour throughout the year making helmets or headpieces, bows, and arrows. The candidate records forced labour at this bounded city-node context without inferring city-wide prevalence, polity-wide practice, or individualized chattel/property status.
claim.notes: Retain Clavijo's source-native term 'captives'. Floor supplies specialist slavery classification but depends on the same passage. Perry and Subtelny support the wider deportation structure, not the exact castle workforce. Do not infer saleability, ownership, heredity, continuity beyond 1404, or a common status for all deported artisans.

territorial_practice.notes: Positive bounded city-node classification from captives compelled to skilled labour year-round. No P-level, population share, polity-wide inference, or generic slavery/property-status strengthening.
